tag: [C] computed in-repo by lib/gust.py — quasi-steady gust loads + morphing-TE alleviation authority. NOT validated; no unsteady (Kussner) or structural dynamics.
question: How much does a vertical gust bump the load factor, and how much of that can the KESTREL-TE morphing law cancel?

method.gust_model: sharp-edged vertical gust, quasi-steady dalpha = atan(w/U)
method.dCl_dA_source: finite difference of lib/morph.py Glauert solver (CLAIM-2 law), alpha=0

claim: CLAIM-3: at the M0.58 cruise point a 50 ft/s (15.24 m/s) sharp-edged vertical gust adds dn = 1.4854 (n = 1 -> 2.485) [C]. The KESTREL-TE law at its demonstrated A = 3% chord droop (dCl = 0.363) cancels 77% of that gust's lift increment; full cancellation needs A = 180.3 mm droop at root chord — just past the demonstrated range, so the law has real gust-alleviation authority but not complete authority at 50 ft/s. Quasi-steady [C]; falsify with unsteady CFD of the morphed wing (actuation rate is the untested part).
caveats: Quasi-steady: real sharp-edged gusts build up over ~chord-lengths of travel (Kussner), so true peak loads are somewhat higher than these numbers.
No structural dynamics: wing bending relief and aeroelastic response not modeled.
Helmbold AR correction is the simple incompressible form; transonic/compressibility ignored.
Morph actuation RATE not modeled — a gust alleviation system must move the TE in ~0.1-0.5 s; that is the falsification path (unsteady CFD + actuator model).
Gust alleviation also reduces passenger-perceived bumpiness, which is the design goal in docs/passenger-first.md — this file quantifies the aerodynamic authority only.
